missing.why: The PoC uses vm.store to set totalAssets. The evidence record says this does not affect the handler-mismatch revert, so it is not required to support the claim.

reason: The report confirms the trigger requires a trusted manager action, which the evidence record identifies as outside the stated scope. It also shows the revert is reversible by restoring the handler; no fund loss or higher severity is demonstrated.
caps: layers disagree: evidence requires obligation 2, 3, the decision does not

evidence.claim: Re-pointing an asset's slashing handler in Core (allowlistAssets) makes NativeVault.slashAssets revert with NotSlashStore, DoSing slashing for already-deployed NativeVaults.
evidence.support_reason: NativeVault.slashAssets requires slashingHandler == self.slashStore (line 308), where slashStore is fixed at initialize (line 75). Core.allowlistAssets (Core.sol:85-91 -> CoreLib.sol:67-75) overwrites assetSlashingHandlers[asset] with no check against existing vaults, and SlasherLib.finalizeSlashing (SlasherLib.sol:135-138) passes self.assetSlashingHandlers[vault.asset()] as the handler. So after a re-point, finalizeSlashing reverts for every NativeVault whose slashStore differs.
preconditions: MANAGER/owner calls allowlistAssets to re-point DEAD_BEEF to a different handler
at least one NativeVault already deployed with the old slashStore
a slashing request is queued/finalized after the re-point

missing_evidence.item: Contest policy does not list MANAGER/OWNER misconfiguration or admin-action DoS as in-scope; the report itself concedes the harm requires a trusted role acting through a normal admin function.
missing_evidence.why: Reachability under allowed actors is the crux. The only trigger is a MANAGER/owner call to allowlistAssets; if the policy treats trusted-role misconfiguration as out of scope, the path is not reachable by an in-scope actor and the finding fails obligation 2.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: The policy (or a judge ruling) explicitly states that a MANAGER/owner re-pointing an allowlisted asset's slashing handler is an in-scope attack surface, or the report shows a permissionless trigger.

missing_evidence.item: Severity justification: the demonstrated effect is a temporary revert of finalizeSlashing that is fully reversible by the same trusted role (restore old handler) or by per-vault implementation upgrade.
missing_evidence.why: The stated impact is DoS of slashing, but the DoS is admin-induced and admin-reversible with no fund loss; the report must show this meets the contest's severity bar for a trusted-role-triggered, self-healing condition.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: The report ties the effect to a specific severity criterion (e.g., a stated invariant that slashing must not be blockable) or the judge accepts admin-reversible DoS as Low/QA.

missing_evidence.item: PoC credits totalAssets via vm.store rather than the beacon-proof flow.
missing_evidence.why: The slashing path under test (finalizeSlashing -> slashAssets -> NotSlashStore check) does not depend on how totalAssets was produced; the revert is independent of balance provenance, so the missing beacon flow does not undermine the claim.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: A test drives totalAssets through validateWithdrawalCredentials/validateSnapshotProofs before slashing.
